messages.subject: Re: Pulling a unique client identifier from the session object (session$token)
messages.subject_clean: Pulling a unique client identifier from the session object (session$token)
messages.body_plain:
Sounds like it should work. It's guaranteed to be unique for each session and to be stable throughout that session.

On Mon, Dec 17, 2018 at 1:23 PM John Harrold <john.m....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I have a Shiny App that writes data on the shiny server based on the individual user connected. If I have logins enabled I can use session$user as a unique value. However if I don't have logins enabled, I'd still like to be able to do this.
>
> It looks like session$token might be what I want. It appears to be md5 hash, but I'm not really sure how it's generated and how it's used. Does it change during a session?
>
> I've looked but I haven't found any documentation on the session object. Does anyone have any place where the different fields of this variable are documented?
>
> Thanks
> John
>

messages.subject: Re: HTML script tag for server output
messages.subject_clean: HTML script tag for server output
messages.body_plain: You can't ever "read" output$id--it's not a place to store values. Instead, create a uiOutput/renderUI whose render expression is tags$script(src = input$xx).
